before.text:
Abstract. There has been a surge of interest of late in an old result of Nyman and
                                                         Beurling giving a Hilbert space formulation of the Riemann hypothesis. Many authors
                                                         have contributed to this circle of ideas, culminating in a beautiful refinement due to
                                                         Baez-Duarte. The purpose of this little survey is to dis-entangle the resulting web of
                                                         complications, and reveal the essential simplicity of the main results.

                                                         Keywords.      Riemann hypothesis; Hilbert space; total set; semigroups.

before.text:
Recall that a set A of vectors in a Hilbert space H is said to be total if the set of all finite
                                             linear combinations of elements of A is dense in H , i.e., if no proper closed subspace
                                             of the Hilbert space contains the set A. In terms of these few notions and notations, the
                                             recent result of Baez-Duarte from [2] can be given the following dramatic formulation.
                                             Theorem 1. The following statements are equivalent:
                                               (i) The Riemann hypothesis,
                                              (ii) γ belongs to the closed linear span of {γl : l = 1, 2, 3, . . . }, and
                                             (iii) the set {γl : l = 1, 2, 3, . . . } is total in H .

after.text:
Since {Gl : l = 1, 2, 3, . . . } ⊆ {Fλ : 0 ≤ λ ≤ 1}, the implication (ii) ⇒ (iii) is trivial. To
prove (iii) ⇒ (i), suppose RH is false. Then there is a zeta-zero ρ ∈ Ω. Since ζ (ρ ) = 0, it
follows that Fλ (ρ ) = 0 for all λ ∈ (0, 1]. Thus the set {Fλ : λ ∈ (0, 1]} (and hence also its
closed linear span) is contained in the proper closed subspace {F ∈ H 2 (Ω): F(ρ ) = 0} of
H 2 (Ω). (It is a closed subspace since evaluation at any fixed ρ ∈ Ω is a continuous linear
functional: H 2 (Ω) is a functional Hilbert space.) Since E belongs to the closed linear
span of this set, it follows that 0 = E(ρ ) = ρ1 . Hence 0 = 1: the ultimate contradiction!
This proves (iii) =⇒ (i).

total subset of M . Thus (ii) =⇒ (iii).
   Lastly, if {gl : l = 1, 2, 3, . . .} is a total subset of M then, in particular its closed linear
span contains 1, and hence the closed linear span of {Gl = −̥(gl )} contains E = ̥(1),
so that RH follows by Theorem 2. Thus (iii) =⇒ (i).

section_entries.mathematical_role: Proves totality with a discrete dilation semigroup and transfers the result unitarily to weighted sequences.

unit_result_entry.title: Sampling on reciprocal integers unitarily transfers totality to weighted sequences
unit_result_entry.why_material: A unitary sampling map sends the constant step function to gamma and each discrete generator to gamma_l, making the opening sequence theorem a direct reformulation and carrying over square-free thinning.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: Includes the definition and both named images of the unitary map plus the square-free refinement.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Discrete dilations upgrade the Baez-Duarte closure criterion to totality
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Theorem 7 combines the reciprocal-indexed closure criterion with a semigroup of isometries whose orbit of the constant function contains a total family of interval indicators, proving the discrete family is total exactly under RH.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Finite-dimensional distance decay is equivalent to RH but Gram formulas resist estimation
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The source converts density into decay of distances to initial finite spans, proposes a strong asymptotic, and explains that the resulting ratio of Gram determinants is explicit yet poorly suited to calculation or estimation, recording both a possible route and its bottleneck.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Isometric or unitary maps preserve the same closure/totality question while progressively changing analytic functions into fractional-part functions, step functions, and weighted sequences.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The exact formulas for both transforms and the step-function sampling identity are scan-dependent; this synthesis establishes source-stated equivalence, not a new proof beyond those bridges.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The unitary sequence criterion makes RH equivalent to vanishing distance from gamma to growing finite spans, suggesting Gram determinants as finite observables of the density problem.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The paper explicitly says the resulting determinant formulas are unsuitable for effective estimation and presents no successful bound.
